breaking_news.headline: Trump is hellbent on tariffs. Here are 5 implications

breaking_news.headline: Rage-giving, innovation and cuts: How public media has survived without federal funds
breaking_news.summary: A year after President Trump signed a law ending six decades of federal funding of public media, it's a time of reinvention, innovation and clear anxiety at public tv and radio stations nationwide.

breaking_news.headline: Oil prices are climbing again. Here's why this time could be different
breaking_news.summary: Oil prices surpassed $100 a barrel last week. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe speaks to Bob McNally, founder of the research firm Rapidan Energy Group, about how the Iran war is disrupting oil supplies.

breaking_news.headline: Toy company CEO shares how Trump's new round of tariffs could affect business
breaking_news.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Jay Foreman of toy importer Basic Fun! about President Trump's latest round of tariffs. The company has paid millions of dollars in import duties under Trump.

breaking_news.headline: Kalshi attacks a Wisconsin law banning election bets as 'voter suppression'
breaking_news.summary: The spat between the leading prediction market company and a key battleground state could be a glimpse into the next major fight between states and the fast-growing industry.

breaking_news.headline: Yes, it's possible to save money while paying off credit card debt. Here's how
breaking_news.summary: In fact, experts recommend it because it can keep you off the hamster wheel of debt. Here's how to find the money in your budget to put toward savings and credit card payments.

breaking_news.headline: AI tokens could become the kilowatt-hour of the AI age
breaking_news.summary: AI companies use tokens to track usage and bill customers. Now economists are using them to track the spread of AI through the economy.

breaking_news.headline: Hong Kong activist allowed to stay in UK after deportation threat
breaking_news.summary: Wu was detained for hours at London's Heathrow Airport last week and refused entry, he told the BBC.

breaking_news.headline: French Navy carries out 'shooting drill' mid interview
breaking_news.summary: Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp says the vessel fired 17 shots as he was giving a BBC interview.

breaking_news.headline: 'A narcissist': Victim's family hits out at Kohberger for challenging murder conviction
breaking_news.summary: The man accused of killing four students in Idaho is taking back his plea, which was made to avoid the death penalty.

breaking_news.headline: Mancini reappointed Italy boss after Pirlo controversy
breaking_news.summary: Roberto Mancini is appointed Italy manager for a second time - just a day after Andrea Pirlo rules himself out of the running for the job and technical director Paolo Maldini resigns.

breaking_news.headline: 'A lover of life' - Seattle pays tribute to food festival shooting victims
breaking_news.summary: Families grieved on Monday as they remembered the three people killed in a shooting at a food festival.

breaking_news.headline: US walks out of UN Security Council meeting during France's remarks
breaking_news.summary: The row sparked after the US joined North Korea and Russia in voting against extending the term of the UN high commissioner for human rights.

breaking_news.headline: The cocaine superhighway from Ecuador to Europe - the BBC reports on gangs and the police fightback
breaking_news.summary: The BBC goes on patrol with Ecuador's police, who are grappling with a huge surge in drug crime.

breaking_news.headline: Gironde wildfires pick up as French region braces for new 40C heatwave
breaking_news.summary: Firefighters are braced for a sharp rise in temperatures on Wednesday, which could complicate the containment of wildfires.

breaking_news.headline: Some people's chats with Claude AI found to be publicly available online

breaking_news.headline: Chip stocks slide in US and Asia as AI jitters rattle investors
breaking_news.summary: Trading on South Korea's Kospi index was paused temporarily on Tuesday morning after slumping by 8%.

breaking_news.headline: Is it time to stop using glue and labels on paper?
breaking_news.summary: Labels and adhesives can prevent paper from being recycled but there's new tech aimed at changing that.

breaking_news.headline: Johnson & Johnson offers up to $5.5bn to settle baby powder lawsuits
